notes: Project-owned uv-cache and npm-cache directories contain downloaded dependency archives, not first-party source terminology. They are excluded from the prose nomenclature scan; import/runtime source and adapter controls remain scanned. workspace_docker_cleanup_checks declares subprocess solely for its explicit opt-in container lifetime qualification; its folded self-test uses injected local fixtures.

The pure harness recipe helpers listed in network_allowed_modules use urllib.parse solely to refuse non-loopback configuration addresses or translate protocol fields. They do not open connections. Actual transport is confined to harness_process_relay and the canonical gateway provider adapters.

harness_process and harness_process_relay are declared internal CLI adapters: the only socket paths are private Unix IPC and sandbox-local HTTP. External model requests remain with the supplied canonical gateway broker. Pinned software, private configuration, request limits, process-tree cancellation and denial of native tools are tested separately from model quality; no public solve realization is enabled by listing these mechanics.

network_allowed: HTTP happens ONLY in a declared provider adapter (ollama_client, mistral_client, openrouter_client, openai_responses_client, and custom_endpoint, which is the ONE parameterised adapter for user-supplied OpenAI-compatible servers rather than a per-server module) or a declared server/demo module; everything else asks the directory. Amended 2026-08-24: the rule was written when one provider existed and said 'the ONE place'. Provider plurality is now a requirement, not a convenience — a single provider's 429 stopped a whole campaign — so the invariant is 'only in a declared adapter', and each adapter is listed above. Adding a provider means adding its adapter here with its reason, never relaxing the rule.

subprocess_allowed: opencode_client is the declared coding-worker adapter; mcp_sdk_transport may start an explicitly registered stdio MCP server; workspace_local runs an explicitly authorized argv inside one restricted root; workspace_optional runs Docker with explicit policy and request authority; smoke_ladder.submit_to_kaggle is a declared external effect; _conformance_scan.scan_min_python_syntax invokes an older interpreter because a newer parser cannot prove the declared Python floor.
eval/exec: never — logic_ast interprets a closed operator set instead.
dynamic imports: explicit lazy public exports, self-test registry plumbing, and optional harness availability discovery only; a dynamic import elsewhere is a registration bypass.
secret patterns scan code AND records — evidence files must be secret-free too.

network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/service_runtime/access_checks.py: Real loopback-only administrator acceptance uses temporary credentials and the existing owned fixture servers. It does not contact external providers or mint hosted keys.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/service_runtime/http.py: The authenticated serving transport owns public Host/Origin checks and loopback-only acceptance. It does not perform customer harness execution.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/service_runtime/http_auth.py: The explicitly configured identity adapter fetches a bounded public key set from the exact host-approved endpoint, refuses redirects, and never forwards the bearer token.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/service_runtime/http_boundary_check: Real HTTP acceptance fixtures use only loopback endpoints and do not authorize external provider requests.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/service_runtime/http_checks.py: Official-client HTTP and Model Context Protocol checks use loopback fixtures, temporary records, and no external provider.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/service_runtime/promotion_checks.py: Promotion code checks. The redemption path itself is a durable record operation and opens no socket; the client library is used only to reach owned loopback listeners that the module starts and stops, so that the served refusal for an unknown and an exhausted code is observed byte for byte rather than asserted, and so that a guessed code is seen reaching the existing failed-attempt limit. No payment provider, identity provider or external network is used.
Owns loopback-only test servers and shuts down their exact socket and worker handles.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/service_runtime/stripe_provider.py: The payment provider adapter permits bounded fixed-origin read-only Stripe requests only under explicit host network authority; discovery and default configuration perform no request.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/service_runtime/stripe_sessions.py: Fixed-origin Stripe session adapter. Explicit host network and session-creation authority, exact tenant/customer/plan binding, durable effect identity and no automatic new-identity retry. It does not grant payment acceptance.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/service_runtime/stripe_session_tran: Real loopback HTTP and explicitly injected provider transport checks. Fixtures do not contact Stripe or create external accounts, sessions or charges.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/decisions/jev_checks.py: Provider serialization tests inject a local HTTP transport and never contact TypeSafe or use a real key.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/decisions/http_transport.py: Bounded decision-provider transport, called only through configured adapters and ModelGateway. Exact host endpoint and credential reference, explicit network/model authority, no proxies, redirects, automatic retries or model-server lifecycle.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/decisions/system_one_checks.py: Explicit provider-shaped fixtures use a real loopback HTTP server, temporary state, and exact owned cleanup. No remote endpoint or real model.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/decisions/configuration.py: Uses urllib.parse for effect-free endpoint validation only. Import-boundary checks prohibit HTTP clients and sockets here; outbound requests are owned solely by decisions/http_transport.py.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/decisions/system_one.py: Uses urllib.parse for effect-free endpoint validation only. Import-boundary checks prohibit HTTP clients and sockets here; outbound requests are owned solely by decisions/http_transport.py.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/service_runtime/browser_identity.py: Host-installed browser identity adapter. Network authority is checked before any key or provider read; the signed issuer, browser-only audience and current user are validated at the configured HTTPS origin. The bounded user request refuses redirects, inherited proxies, oversized or duplicate-key responses. It cannot authorize the MCP resource audience.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/service_runtime/browser_identity_ch: Real loopback-only identity acceptance with locally signed tokens, owned temporary listeners and an injected current-user transport. No remote identity account, email, credential or provider request is used.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/service_runtime/account_email.py: Account sign-up and password recovery adapter. Two fixed-origin requests only, each under explicit host network authority: one to the identity provider's administration interface that generates a link without sending a message, and one to the mail provider's send interface. Each request is sent once and never repeated after an uncertain answer; redirects, inherited proxy settings, oversized and non-object answers are refused. Discovery and the default configuration perform no request.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/service_runtime/account_email_check: Account email checks. The adapter itself runs with injected transports; the two real transport functions are exercised against owned loopback listeners that the module starts and stops, so that redirect refusal, the response ceiling and the deadline are observed rather than asserted. No identity provider, mail provider, real address or external network is used.
network_allowed_modules_reasons.core/service_runtime/observability_check: Real loopback-only acceptance for the request reference, the failure journal and the measured readiness answer. It drives the owned temporary fixture server over loopback so that the privacy guard can read every byte of the durable store afterwards. No external provider, remote account or hosted credential is used.
